title: Accounts
content:
On DigitalOcean, you manage your infrastructure and billing with [teams](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/index.html.md). Your personal account on DigitalOcean lets you manage your team membership and your name, sign-in method, and email subscriptions.

[How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/settings/index.html.md): The My Account page lets you view and edit your login method, 2FA, team membership, and email preferences.

[How to Change the Control Panel Theme](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/theme/index.html.md): The control panel theme sets the DigitalOcean Control Panel to a light or dark appearance or matches your operating system’s appearance setting.

[How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/2fa/index.html.md): Use 2FA to add an additional layer of security against unauthorized access to your DigitalOcean account.

[DigitalOcean Teams](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/index.html.md): Teams are how you manage your billing and infrastructure on DigitalOcean. You can work by yourself by remaining the only person on your team or collaborate by adding more people to teams you own.

[How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/deactivate/index.html.md): Deactivate an account to stop billing and prohibit future resource creation. Optionally purge your account data to permanently remove the account from DigitalOcean and prevent account reactivation.

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings
title: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings
content:
# How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings

**Note**:

  DigitalOcean’s terms of service prohibit accounts registered to addresses from OFAC-sanctioned countries. For more information, including a list of countries, see section 5.7 of our **Rules of Conduct** in [our terms of service](https://www.digitalocean.com/legal/terms-of-service-agreement/).

You can edit account information and settings, like your name, password, sign-in method, two-factor authentication, team membership, and email subscriptions.

To access your account settings, go to the [DigitalOcean Control Panel](https://cloud.digitalocean.com), in the top right corner, click the profile icon, and then click **My Account** to go to your [**My Account** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/profile).

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Name
title: Name
content:
## Name

At the top of the **Profile** tab, the **Name** section displays the name on your account. Click the **Edit** button to change it.

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Sign-in Method
title: Sign-in Method
content:
## Sign-in Method

The **Sign-in method** section lets you choose how you log in to your DigitalOcean account. You can use:

- Email and password, including Gmail SSO
- GitHub SSO

To change the sign-in method, click **Change** to open the dropdown menu, and then select the option you want to use.

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Sign-in Method > Email Address and Password
title: Email Address and Password
content:
### Email Address and Password

If you currently use email and password to sign in, you can choose **Update email address** to change your email address.

Enter your new email address into **Enter new email address** field. Then enter your current password into **Confirm password** field to confirm the change. Click **Update** to submit the change.

We send a confirmation email to your new email address to finalize the change. The change does not take effect until you click the link in the confirmation email.

For security reasons, we don’t display your password in the Control Panel. Click **Reset Password** to change your password. If you don’t remember your current password, after clicking **Reset Password**, you can click **Reset Via Email**.

If you’re using an email and password to log in to DigitalOcean, the **Two-factor authentication** section lets you enable or disable [two-factor authentication (2FA)](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/2fa/index.html.md). 2FA adds an extra layer of security to your account by requiring you to provide a code along with your username and password when you log in.

[How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/2fa/index.html.md): Use 2FA to add an additional layer of security against unauthorized access to your DigitalOcean account.

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Sign-in Method > Google or GitHub Accounts
title: Google or GitHub Accounts
content:
### Google or GitHub Accounts

If you currently sign in with a Google or GitHub account, the account email address is displayed in the **Sign-in method** section.

To switch to another account with the same provider, you need to switch to a different login option and then switch back to select a different account.

**Note**:

  To use GitHub SSO, the email addresses on your GitHub account and your DigitalOcean account must match. If you change your GitHub email address before changing your DigitalOcean email address first, you cannot use GitHub to log in to DigitalOcean.

When using Google or GitHub to sign into DigitalOcean, we strongly recommend that you enable two-factor authentication on your [Google](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/9096865) or [GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/free-pro-team@latest/github/authenticating-to-github/securing-your-account-with-two-factor-authentication-2fa) account.

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Email Preferences
title: Email Preferences
content:
## Email Preferences

The **Email subscriptions** section includes a link to the [Subscriptions Preference Center](https://anchor.digitalocean.com/Email_Preferences.html), which lets you opt in or out of the emails you receive from us.

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Your Teams
title: Your Teams
content:
## Your Teams

The **Your teams** section lists any [DigitalOcean Teams](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/index.html.md) you are part of. The team **name**, your **role** (member, biller, or owner), **status** (invited or joined), and join date (if applicable) are listed in the table.

![Your Teams list displaying a single team, showing the user as a member.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/accounts/your-teams.92c0b10cf68898965b822e3a4219a129c7254b886d76ce3a232cd24074df5dc7.png)

The **…** menu next to each team has several options:

- **Go to team** switches to the team account and returns you to the control panel.
- If you are a team owner, **Manage team settings** takes you to the team settings page.
- If you are a team owner or biller, **Manage billing** takes you to the team billing page.
- **Leave team** opens a window to confirm that you want to leave the team. If you are the last owner on a team, leaving the team deletes the team and charges the payment method associated with the team for the team’s final balance.

You can also **Create a Team** in this section.

heading_path: How to Manage DigitalOcean Personal Account Settings > Deactivate Account
title: Deactivate Account
content:
## Deactivate Account

[How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/deactivate/index.html.md): Deactivate an account to stop billing and prohibit future resource creation. Optionally purge your account data to permanently remove the account from DigitalOcean and prevent account reactivation.

The **Deactivate Account** section allows you to deactivate your account and purge all your account data, including email addresses and payment information.

Before you deactivate your account, you must delete or transfer ownership of any teams your team you own and resolve any outstanding bills.

heading_path: How to Change the Control Panel Theme
title: How to Change the Control Panel Theme
content:
# How to Change the Control Panel Theme

The theme controls whether the [DigitalOcean Control Panel](https://cloud.digitalocean.com) displays with a light or dark appearance. You can select a theme directly or have the control panel match your operating system’s appearance setting. Your selection is saved as a personal preference.

To change the theme, in the top right corner of the control panel, click the profile icon, and then click **Theme**.

![The control panel profile menu with the Theme option visible below Feature Preview.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/accounts/theme-menu.5bf64ed9bb3210594a01baca27d2d0ed816c8940dbdfcc2106ba8ac06bbf0dd0.png)

In the **Theme** menu, select one of the following options:

- **Light** displays the control panel with a light background.
- **Dark** displays the control panel with a dark background.
- **Auto** (default) matches the control panel to your operating system’s appearance setting and switches automatically when your system changes between light and dark.

![The Theme menu showing the Light, Dark, and Auto options with Light selected.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/accounts/theme-options.0a32237ea5cd072d8fdaeefe529c986600731775699eb1983552615a91a6b0e5.png)

The control panel applies your selection immediately, and a checkmark indicates the active theme.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts
title: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts
content:
# How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts

If you log in to DigitalOcean with a username and password, enabling 2FA adds an additional layer of security against unauthorized access to your account.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Learn more about two-factor authentication.
title: Learn more about two-factor authentication.
content:
## Learn more about two-factor authentication.

An *authentication factor* is a piece of information used to verify that you’re allowed to do something, like a [keycard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keycard_lock) used to unlock a hotel door.

This is one way of characterizing authentication factors:

- **Something you know**: This is private knowledge that only you have, like a password or a PIN.
- **Something you have**: This is a physical object that only you have, like a phone, a key, or a bank card.
- **Something you are**: This is a physical characteristic that only you have, like your fingerprint or your voice.

*Two-factor authentication*, commonly abbreviated as 2FA, is any form of verification that requires two factors, like withdrawing money from an ATM using both a [bank card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATM_card) (something you have) and its [PIN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_identification_number) (something you know).

A common first factor for online accounts is a password (something you know). A common second factor is an authentication code from an app on your phone (something you have).

We strongly recommend enabling 2FA on all DigitalOcean accounts.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Default Account Authentication
title: Default Account Authentication
content:
## Default Account Authentication

When you first create your account, 2FA is disabled, but DigitalOcean takes other steps to protect your account.

Each time you log in from a new location using a new device or a different web browser, we email an authorization code to the address linked to your account. You need to check your email, retrieve the code, and enter it to complete your login.

Even without 2FA enabled, a bad actor would need both your DigitalOcean password and your email password to log in. This isn’t as effective as 2FA, but it increases the difficulty for would-be attackers and provides you with notification if someone is trying to access your account.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication
title: Enabling Two-Factor Authentication
content:
## Enabling Two-Factor Authentication

To enable 2FA for your DigitalOcean account, log in to [the DigitalOcean Control Panel](https://cloud.digitalocean.com), in the top right corner, click the profile icon, and then click **My Account** to go to your [**My Account** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/profile).

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Choosing the Second Factor
title: Choosing the Second Factor
content:
### Choosing the Second Factor

Scroll to the **Two-factor authentication** section, and then click **Set Up 2FA**.

**Note**:

  2FA is available only when you log in to DigitalOcean with a username and password. If you [log in with Google or GitHub](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/settings/index.html.md#sso), you manage 2FA with your [Google](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/9096865) or [GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/free-pro-team@latest/github/authenticating-to-github/securing-your-account-with-two-factor-authentication-2fa) account instead of your DigitalOcean account.

In the **Set up two factor authentication** window, choose your second factor and a backup method. Under the **Choose Method** section, choose your authentication method (either using an authentication app or using SMS).

![Window showing the two factor authentication method options](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/accounts/set-up.976a9b9b2f74b5c637912227fc48dfd0397c85b7c40239f371a1ee545dec3e8c.png)

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Using an Authentication App (Recommended)
title: Using an Authentication App (Recommended)
content:
### Using an Authentication App (Recommended)

Authenticator apps like [Google Authenticator](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/1066447?hl=en), [Authy](https://authy.com/), [1Password](https://1password.com/), [Microsoft Authenticator](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/account/authenticator), and [Duo](https://duo.com/) are small, free mobile applications used to generate security codes. They work globally and are more secure than SMS because they don’t transmit the security codes across the network.

When you choose this method, you need to scan the provided QR code using the authenticator app on your phone or tablet. This links your device to your DigitalOcean account.

If you’re unable to scan the QR code, click the **Try this instead** link directly underneath it to get a numerical code which you can enter manually. Follow the directions in your specific authenticator app to enter the code, then enter the PIN that the app gives you in the field provided. Once you’ve entered the PIN, the app links with your DigitalOcean account.

Once your DigitalOcean account and 2FA app are linked, when you log in to DigitalOcean, you need to open the app and enter the code provided in the control panel to finish logging in.

Some authenticator apps have features like backups and syncing to help you restore access to the app if you lose your device. We recommend using these features for added reliability.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Using SMS
title: Using SMS
content:
### Using SMS

If you select SMS, your mobile carrier must be able to deliver a text message, which means you need mobile signal or an internet connection. This may be inconvenient when traveling internationally. In addition, because SMS messages are vulnerable to being intercepted by hackers, they’re not as secure as an app. However, using SMS for 2FA still provides much stronger security for your account than not enabling 2FA at all.

When you select SMS, you are prompted for the phone number.

**Note**:

  You cannot use VoIP or Telephony telephone numbers from services like Google Voice or Ooma.

Once you enter the code, DigitalOcean sends a code via SMS. When you receive it, enter the code to link your phone and your account. From then on, you receive codes via SMS to enter into the control panel to complete your login.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Choosing a Backup Method
title: Choosing a Backup Method
content:
### Choosing a Backup Method

Once you’ve configured your primary method for 2FA, you need to add a backup method. This is how you can regain access to your account if your 2FA device is lost or stolen.

You can use backup codes or an authenticator app. We recommend using backup codes.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Backup Codes (Recommended)
title: Backup Codes (Recommended)
content:
### Backup Codes (Recommended)

Backup codes act like a second password, so store them in a secure place that you can access without your phone.

Backup codes are visible on-screen when you enable 2FA. You can also download a `.txt` file called **digitalocean_backupcodes.txt**.

Backup codes are single use, so it can be helpful to delete or cross out a backup code once you use it. If you only have a few valid backup codes left, you can generate more. When you regenerate backup codes, any remaining codes from before are no longer valid.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Enabling Two-Factor Authentication > Authenticator App
title: Authenticator App
content:
### Authenticator App

You can use an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Duo as your backup solution.

We do not recommend this because it is phone-based, and only selectable as a backup option if you select SMS as your primary 2FA solution. In the scenario where you can’t access your SMS messages and need to use a backup method, your phone might not be a valid option to use due to whatever is preventing SMS access.

For this reason, we recommend using an authenticator app as your primary 2FA method with backup codes.

When two-factor authentication is enabled, the **Two-factor authentication** section displays your default authentication method and your backup method.

![The Two-Factor Authentication section of the My Account page](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/accounts/2fa-when-enabled.cb640835ee008642a60f4673543aab4f254675cd09027ddbc147b98fd53a6a80.png)

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Disabling Two-Factor Authentication
title: Disabling Two-Factor Authentication
content:
## Disabling Two-Factor Authentication

You can disable 2FA on the [**My Account** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/profile), in the **Two-factor authentication** section. Click **Disable 2FA** to disable two-factor authentication.

If you lose access to your 2FA device or can’t receive the code via SMS, try searching your computer for the backup codes text file named `digitalocean_backupcodes.txt` by default. If your backup method is not functioning, [submit a ticket to the DigitalOcean support team](https://www.digitalocean.com/company/contact/support) for help restoring access to your account.

heading_path: How to Manage Two-Factor Authentication for DigitalOcean Accounts > Switching Authenticator Apps
title: Switching Authenticator Apps
content:
## Switching Authenticator Apps

If you have enabled 2FA for your account and are using an authentication app, you can change the current app you are using to authenticate your DigitalOcean account by disabling 2FA and then enabling it again using your preferred authentication app.

To switch your authentication app, follow the steps above to first [disable 2FA](#disabling-two-factor-authentication) for your account, then [enable 2FA](#enabling-two-factor-authentication) again using your new authentication app.

heading_path: How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data
title: How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data
content:
# How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data

Deactivating an account stops billing and prohibits future resource creation. You can choose to reactivate the account in the future with the same account history, resource limits, and verification status.

When you deactivate an account, you have the option to permanently remove the account’s data from DigitalOcean, including email and billing information. Purging this data means you cannot reactivate the account in the future, so you would need to create and verify a new account to use DigitalOcean again.

heading_path: How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data > Resolving Team Memberships
title: Resolving Team Memberships
content:
## Resolving Team Memberships

Before you deactivate your account, you must resolve your team memberships:

- **If you are the sole owner of any teams with additional members**, you must either [delete the teams](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/delete/index.html.md) or [assign a different team owner](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/manage-membership/index.html.md#modify-existing-members).
- **If you are an owner of a team with that has at least one additional owner**, you are automatically removed from the team when you deactivate your account.
- **If you are the only member of a team**, the team is automatically deleted when you deactivate your account.

When you delete a team, you must destroy all resources on the team. The payment method associated with the team is be charged for the team’s final balance.

heading_path: How to Deactivate DigitalOcean Accounts and Purge Account Data > Deactivating an Account
title: Deactivating an Account
content:
## Deactivating an Account

To deactivate your account, go to the [DigitalOcean Control Panel](https://cloud.digitalocean.com), in the top right corner, click the profile icon, and then click **My Account** to go to your [**My Account** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/profile).

Scroll to the **Deactivate account** section, on the right, click **Deactivate**, and then click **Deactivate Account**.

If you are the sole owner of any teams with additional members, this takes you to the **Before You Deactivate** page, which lists the steps you must take before you can deactivate your account. For example, deleting team resources or transferring ownership of teams.

![Account deactivation page showing a table of teams where the user is an owner, with warnings about required actions before deactivation.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/accounts/before-you-deactivate.21b8f32056b470435ab3e1c9f121c9444ab0b682dc5d92b9cc947798eddd73c7.png)

As you resolve issues, click **Refresh** to see your progress.

Once your account is ready for deactivation, clicking **Refresh** takes you to the **Deactivate My Account** page.

![Deactivate Account page showing an option to purge account data and a table listing teams the user owns, with notes about teams being deleted or the user being removed before deactivation.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/accounts/deactivate-account.25bec1a7ca18003ba2b4c8a157d9b011ef27c6990dc868cfd1311741ce00d707.png)

You also have the option to permanently remove a deactivated account’s data from DigitalOcean:

- If you do not check the box next to **Purge all of my account data**, you can reactivate the same account in the future. This keeps the account history and resource limits.
- If you check the box next to **Purge all of my account data**, you lose this data permanently. To use DigitalOcean again, you need to create a new account and go through the verification process again.

Select your option, then click **Deactivate Account**, which deactivates your account and takes you either to the account reactivation page (if you didn’t purge your data) or to the login page (if you did purge your data). After deactivation, a link to a survey asks how we can improve the platform.

title: DigitalOcean Teams
content:
# DigitalOcean Teams

On DigitalOcean, you manage your infrastructure and billing with teams. You can group related teams into [organizations](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/index.html.md) for consolidated billing, payment, and invoicing. Your [personal account](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/accounts/index.html.md) lets you manage your team membership and your name, sign-in method, and email subscriptions.

When you sign up for DigitalOcean, you are the only member of your default team. You can always work by yourself on a team of one.

You can also collaborate with others by inviting them to teams you own. Teams are available at no cost and you can create multiple teams with any number of team members. Each team has separate billing and its own payment information unless it belongs to an organization.

[Team Roles](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/roles/index.html.md): Each team member has a role which determines their permissions on the team. Permissions grant varying levels of access to the team’s shared resources, billing information, and settings.

[Team Settings](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/settings/index.html.md): Team settings let you choose a team contact email and enable secure sign-in for all team members.

[Team How-Tos](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/index.html.md): Step-by-step instructions on how to perform specific tasks with DigitalOcean Teams.

[Team Limits](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/limits/index.html.md): Limits and known issues for DigitalOcean Teams.

title: 13 March 2026
content:
### 13 March 2026

- [Team owners and resource modifiers](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/roles/index.html.md) can now view resource usage and limits in the DigitalOcean Control Panel. You can use this interface to understand resource capacity, manage resource growth, and initiate support requests to increase limits when needed. For more information, see [View Resource Limits](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/view-resource-limits/index.html.md).

title: 11 March 2026
content:
### 11 March 2026

- Teams and organizations now support dedicated billing and security contact emails. Team and organization owners can add email addresses to receive billing or security notifications independently from the default team or organization contact email. See [team contact emails](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/settings/contact-emails/index.html.md) and [organization contact emails](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/how-to/manage-organization/index.html.md#manage-contact-emails).

title: 20 January 2026
content:
### 20 January 2026

- We have enabled silent re-authentication for [single sign-on (SSO)](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/configure-sso/index.html.md) when using the DigitalOcean Control Panel. DigitalOcean automatically refreshes the identity provider (IdP) access tokens, so you are no longer unexpectedly logged out when the tokens expire. This improves security and minimizes interruptions to your workflow.

For more information, see [the full release notes](https://docs.digitalocean.com/release-notes/index.html.md).

title: Team Roles
content:
# Team Roles

Each team member has a role which determines their permissions on the team. Permissions grant varying levels of access to the team’s shared resources, billing information, and settings.

title: DigitalOcean Organizations
content:
# DigitalOcean Organizations

Organizations are groupings of related [teams](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/index.html.md). Organizations enable consolidated billing, payment, and invoicing, and provide detailed spend breakdowns by team. Organization owners can manage members, settings, and billing across teams in the organization while team owners can manage their team’s resources and view spending.

Organizations are available at no cost.

title: Organizations and Teams
content:
## Organizations and Teams

Teams are where you create and manage resources, like Droplets and databases. An organization sits above teams: it holds one or more teams and consolidates their billing, but it does not contain resources directly.

When a team [joins an organization](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/how-to/manage-teams/index.html.md):

- **Billing consolidates at the organization level.** The organization’s payment methods, billing address, billing settings, alerts, and tax information replace the team’s, and the organization receives a single invoice covering all of its teams. Joining an organization is permanent, and a team can belong to only one organization.
- **Resource management stays in the team.** You continue to create and manage Droplets, databases, and other resources within each team. The organization dashboard does not list or manage resources.
- **Membership and roles remain independent at each level.** [Organization roles](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/roles/predefined/index.html.md) (owner, admin, and biller) control access to organization settings, membership, and billing. [Team roles](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/roles/index.html.md) control access to a team’s resources and settings. Organization membership does not grant access to a team’s resources unless the user is also a member of that team.

The following table summarizes what each level manages:

| Level | Manages | Billing |
|---|---|---|
| Team | Resources, team membership and roles, team settings | Uses the organization’s payment methods and settings when the team belongs to an organization |
| Organization | Teams, organization membership and roles, organization settings | Consolidated payment methods, invoices, prepayments, and spend alerts for all teams in the organization |

heading_path: How to Pay Your Bill > Payment Methods and Due Dates
title: Payment Methods and Due Dates
content:
## Payment Methods and Due Dates

DigitalOcean billing cycles are monthly. Your balance accrues over the course of the calendar month based on your resource usage. Your balance is due on the first day of each month.

If your team belongs to an [organization](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/index.html.md), DigitalOcean bills the organization for the usage of all of its teams. Prepayments, automatic charges, and payments apply at the organization level.

**Note**:

  If your team or organization does not have a payment history yet, your balance may be due mid-month when it reaches your tier’s auto-charge amount. Each tier has a prepayment amount and an auto-charge amount that determine when we collect outstanding usage. As you build payment history over time with successful, non-zero invoices, your tier and limits can increase automatically. For the full tier table and more detail, see [View Resource Limits](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/view-resource-limits/index.html.md#view-resource-limits).

There are two ways to pay for your resource usage:

- At any time during the month, you can [manually make a payment](#now) using any valid payment method.

  This lets you pay for your month-to-date resource usage before it’s due, pay an overdue balance, or make a prepayment. Prepayments let you pay ahead of time for future resource usage. A one-time prepayment can increase [your trust tier and unlock higher limits immediately](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/view-resource-limits/index.html.md).
- When your balance is due, we first apply any prepayments, then we automatically charge the primary payment method on your team or organization for the remaining balance.

The following table shows the resource tiers, prepayment amount, and auto-charge amounts.

| Tier | Prepayment amount | Auto-charge amount |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | No Prepay | $25 |
| Tier 2 | $50 | $50 |
| Tier 3 | $250 | $250 |
| Tier 4 | $1,000 | $1,000 |
| Tier 5 | $4,000 | $4,000 |

We currently accept payment using credit cards (Visa, MasterCard, American Express, Discover, UnionPay, Diners Club, and JCB), debit cards, and third-party providers (including PayPal, Google Pay, and Apple Pay). For qualifying customers, we also support ACH direct debit from U.S. banks.

[How to Manage Payment Methods on DigitalOcean](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/manage-payment-methods/index.html.md): How to add, edit, and remove payment methods on your team, including credit cards, debit cards, crypto wallets, and third-party providers.

heading_path: How to Pay Your Bill > Making a Payment
title: Making a Payment
content:
## Making a Payment

You can make a manual payment on [the **Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing). Your current balance is listed at the top of the page, next to a payment button. The text of the button varies if the balance is overdue or if you’re making an early payment.

For organizations, you can make a payment from the organization’s billing overview. Click the profile icon in the top right of the Control Panel, click **View Organizations**, select your organization, then click the **Billing** tab. Click **Make a payment** to pay a balance, or **Add funds** to make a prepayment.

Click the payment button to go to the [**Make a payment** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/pay-now). In the **Payment Amount** section, you can select from any past due balance, estimated costs for the current billing period, or a custom amount.

After you enter the amount you want to pay, you can make the payment in two ways:

- **Saved Payment Methods**. You can choose from any credit card, debit card, crypto wallet, or third-party provider that you have already saved to the team. You can also add a new credit or debit card with the **Add card** option in the drop-down menu.

  To use this option, select or add a card, then click **Submit Payment** to pay.
- **Pay with a 3rd-Party Provider**. You can submit a one-time payment with a third-party provider, like PayPal, Google Pay, or Apple Pay. To use this option, click the third-party provider you want to use, then complete the transaction after you are rerouted to that provider.

  When using PayPal, your balance updates after your payment is processed, which often takes several hours due to PayPal’s processing. PayPal also sometimes holds payments for up to 72 hours, meaning PayPal has received your money but hasn’t sent it to us yet, but the payment still applies once PayPal releases it.

If you pay by ACH credit, the payment takes longer to process than card or third-party payments. Your balance updates only after we receive the funds from your bank, which can take several business days.

heading_path: How to Pay Your Bill > Serverless Inference Auto-Reload
title: Serverless Inference Auto-Reload
content:
## Serverless Inference Auto-Reload

[Serverless Inference](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/how-to/si-overview/index.html.md) requires a positive prepaid account balance and deducts usage charges from it. This balance is shared across your entire account, so charges from other DigitalOcean products also draw from it. However, Serverless Inference is the only product DigitalOcean suspends when the balance reaches $0. For details, see [How Other Products Affect Your Prepayment Balance](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/how-to/manage-serverless-inference-prepayment/index.html.md#shared-balance).

To avoid a service interruption when this balance runs low, you can enable auto-reload, which automatically adds a set amount to your account prepayment when your balance reaches a threshold you choose. Auto-reload charges your primary payment method first, then your backup payment method if the first attempt fails. For setup steps, see [Manage Serverless Inference Prepayment](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/how-to/manage-serverless-inference-prepayment/index.html.md#enable-auto-reload).

# How to Manage Payment Methods on DigitalOcean

You can [add](#add), [edit](#edit), and [delete](#delete) your team’s payment methods on [the **Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing) in the **Payment methods** section.

Teams that belong to an [organization](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/index.html.md) use the organization’s payment methods instead of their own. To create resources or invite additional team members, you need to add a payment method to your team.

heading_path: How to Manage Payment Methods on DigitalOcean > Accepted Payment Methods
title: Accepted Payment Methods
content:
## Accepted Payment Methods

DigitalOcean accepts the following payment methods:

- **Credit and debit cards**. We accept Visa, MasterCard, American Express, Discover, UnionPay, Diners Club, and JCB credit cards.

  Credit and debit cards from India need to be enabled for international transactions. Cards issued by Citibank, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, IndusInd Bank, RBL Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank are less likely to be declined than other banks.
- **Third-party providers**, like PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay, Alipay, and Link.
- **Crypto wallets**. We accept stablecoin payments from over 400 wallets. Access to the crypto payment method is currently limited and may not be available to all customers in all locations.
- **ACH direct debit** for qualifying customers with U.S. bank accounts.

We do not accept virtual, electron, or prepaid cards.

When you have more than one payment method saved to your team, the first one you add becomes the default payment method, and any additional payment methods you add are marked as backups. We charge your default payment method automatically each billing cycle. You can [update your default payment method](#default) at any time.

heading_path: How to Manage Payment Methods on DigitalOcean > Adding a Payment Method
title: Adding a Payment Method
content:
## Adding a Payment Method

heading_path: How to Manage Payment Methods on DigitalOcean > Adding a Payment Method > Bank Account (ACH)
title: Bank Account (ACH)
content:
### Bank Account (ACH)

Before setting up ACH direct debit on DigitalOcean, we strongly recommend [providing Stripe’s company IDs](https://support.stripe.com/questions/ach-direct-debit-company-ids-for-stripe) to your bank. Stripe explains:

> \[S]ome business bank accounts may have filters in place to deny debits from unknown entities. To allow Stripe to debit from or deposit into your (or your customer’s) account on your behalf, Stripe’s ACH company IDs must be provided to the bank to ensure ACH transactions will be processed.
>
> In some cases, a debit that is attempted on such an account without providing Stripe’s ACH company IDs will result in an unexpected dispute. When this happens, the bank account may also become blocked for use with Stripe.

To connect a bank account for ACH direct debit payments, click **US bank account**. You can instantly verify your bank using OAuth.

Alternatively, you can manually enter your bank details. When you manually enter details, in the next few business days, we make two small micro-deposits to your bank account. Within ten days of receiving them, you must verify your bank account by entering the micro-deposit amounts either on the DigitalOcean billing page or on the Stripe page via the link we email to you.

Once you add a bank account, ACH direct debit becomes the default payment method on your team. To change the default payment method, you need to remove the bank account as a payment method.

For more information, including a list of countries, see section 5.7 of our **Rules of Conduct** in [our terms of service](https://www.digitalocean.com/legal/terms-of-service-agreement/).

title: Late Payments
content:
# Late Payments

DigitalOcean has a monthly billing cycle. On the first calendar day of each month, we [invoice](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/invoices/index.html.md) and charge accounts for the previous month’s resource usage, applying [signup credit](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/signup-credit/index.html.md) and [taxes](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/taxes/index.html.md) when applicable.

Depending on your account tier, we may also charge your primary payment method earlier in the month when your outstanding balance reaches your tier’s auto-charge amount. This charge is automatic. For current prepayment and auto-charge amounts by tier, see [View Resource Limits](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/teams/how-to/view-resource-limits/index.html.md#view-resource-limits) or the [**Resource Limits** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/limits) in the Control Panel. For how due dates and tiers work together, see [How to Pay Your Bill](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/pay-bills/index.html.md#payment-methods-and-due-dates).

When we charge an account, we first apply any [PayPal prepayments](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/pay-bills/index.html.md#payment-methods-and-due-dates) to the balance.

If there is a balance remaining after prepayments, we charge the account’s default [credit or debit card](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/manage-payment-methods/index.html.md). If the default payment method fails, we try charging other payment methods on file.

title: When Enforcement Starts
content:
## When Enforcement Starts

If we cannot collect an outstanding balance, for example, after a monthly charge on the first day of the month fails or after a mid-month charge at your tier’s auto-charge amount fails, the same enforcement process applies.

title: Past Due Accounts
content:
## Past Due Accounts

If there are no valid payment methods on file to cover an outstanding balance, the account is past due, at which point:

- We email the account owner.
- We place the account on hold, which prevents creating new resources.
- The account’s existing resources continue to run.
- In certain cases, any [Spaces](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/spaces/index.html.md) on the account cannot be accessed.

To restore a past due account, the account owner needs to log in and [pay the balance](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/pay-bills/index.html.md).

title: Suspended Accounts
content:
## Suspended Accounts

If an account continues to remain past due, we email the account owner and the account is suspended, at which point:

- We power down the account’s resources.
- We redirect logins to the payment page.

To restore a suspended account, the account owner needs to log in and [pay the balance](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/pay-bills/index.html.md).

title: Permanently Deleted Resources
content:
## Permanently Deleted Resources

If an unresolved balance continues after suspension, we may permanently delete the account’s resources. Deleted resources cannot be recovered. The account owner can still pay the balance to access the account, but they must recreate any resources that were removed.

How fast an account moves between past due, suspension, and permanent deletion depends on the account. DigitalOcean does not publish fixed timelines for these stages.

title: Spend Alerts
content:
# Spend Alerts

Spend alerts send email notifications when spending on your team or organization crosses a percentage threshold of a monthly budget you define. You can create multiple alerts with different scopes: total spend, specific products, or, for organizations, specific teams.

Spend alerts are available for both teams and [organizations](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/index.html.md):

- For teams, go to [the **Spend alerts** tab](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing/spend-alerts) on the **Billing** page.
- For organizations, click the profile icon in the top right of the Control Panel, click **View Organizations**, select your organization, click the **Billing** tab, then click **Spend alerts**.

heading_path: Spend Alerts > Create a Spend Alert
title: Create a Spend Alert
content:
## Create a Spend Alert

To create a spend alert, click **Create alert** to open the **Create New Spend Alert** window, then fill out the following fields:

- **Alert name**: A name for the alert.
- **Monthly budget amount**: The monthly spend amount that percentage thresholds are measured against.
- **Alert thresholds**: One or more percentages of your budget. We send a notification when your usage crosses each threshold. To use a percentage not in the list, click **Add custom threshold**.
- **What do you want to track?**: Choose **Total spend** to track all usage in the alert’s scope, or **Specific products** to narrow the alert to products you choose.

For organizations, an alert’s scope can cover the entire organization or a single team in the organization.

The **Notification recipients** section lists who receives the alert emails: team owners and billers for team alerts, and organization owners and billers for organization alerts.

Click **Create alert** to save the alert.

**Note**:

  A spend alert budget is not a spending cap and does not limit how much you can use. Separately from any alerts you set, we attempt to charge your payment method when your usage reaches your tier’s [auto-charge amount](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/pay-bills/index.html.md#payment-methods-and-due-dates). If a charge fails, your access to provisioning resources is restricted until payment is resolved. You can view the current amount due on the [**Billing**](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing) page.

heading_path: Spend Alerts > Edit a Spend Alert
title: Edit a Spend Alert
content:
## Edit a Spend Alert

To edit an existing alert, on the **Spend alerts** page, click the **…** menu next to the alert, then click **Edit alert** to open the **Edit Spend Alert** page. Update the alert’s name, budget, thresholds, or tracking options, then click **Save changes**.

heading_path: Spend Alerts > How Spend Alert Notifications Work
title: How Spend Alert Notifications Work
content:
## How Spend Alert Notifications Work

We send notifications based on your actual usage and notify recipients within an hour of your spend crossing a threshold. Each threshold notifies once per billing cycle. If you change an alert’s budget or thresholds during a billing cycle, its threshold tracking resets, and notifications can fire again as spend crosses the updated thresholds.

Because alerts are based on actual usage, projections of Droplet transfer in excess of the transfer pool do not trigger an alert until they are applied to the invoice.

title: Migrated Billing Alerts
content:
## Migrated Billing Alerts

Before spend alerts, you could set a single billing alert that emailed you when your monthly spending exceeded a set amount. If you had a billing alert, we migrated it to the **Spend alerts** page as an alert named **Account Spend Alert** with a single threshold at 100% of your previous alert amount. To receive notifications before your spending reaches that amount, edit the alert and add lower thresholds.

title: Invoices
content:
# Invoices

DigitalOcean billing cycles are monthly. On the first day of each month, we invoice and charge your team’s or organization’s primary payment method for the previous month’s usage. Teams that belong to an [organization](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/index.html.md) are billed together on the organization’s invoice. Organizations receive an invoice if at least one team in the organization used resources during the billing cycle. Teams that do not belong to an organization receive an invoice only if the team itself used resources.

Invoices include the following information:

- Charges the team or organization has accrued in a billing cycle, like resource usage
- [Credits](#credits) applied to the invoice, if any
- [Discounts](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/discounts/index.html.md) applied to the invoice, if any
- [Purchase orders](#purchase-orders), if any
- Reference information, like the invoice number, payment due date, and the name and email address on the team or organization

You can update the organization or team information displayed on invoices. For teams, use the **Billing** page’s [**Settings** tab](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing/settings). For organizations, click the profile icon in the top right of the Control Panel, click **View Organizations**, select your organization, then open **Billing Settings** in the **Billing** tab. Any changes you make are immediately visible on invoices you view thereafter.

title: View and Download Invoices
content:
## View and Download Invoices

When we create an invoice, we email a PDF of it to team members with the owner or biller role. For organizations, we email the PDF to organization members with the owner or biller role, as well as any verified [billing contacts](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/organizations/how-to/manage-organization/index.html.md#manage-contact-emails). Invoices are also available directly in the Control Panel, as a downloadable PDF, and as a downloadable CSV file.

**Note**:

  For a daily breakdown of spend over a custom date range, see the [**Insights** tab on the **Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing/insights). The [Spend by Date Range report](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/spend-by-date-range/index.html.md) groups spend by product and highlights your top resources. You can also retrieve daily spend data through the [Billing API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/billing/index.html.md).

On the [**Overview** tab of the **Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing), your latest invoice is visible in the **Month-to-date Summary** section:

![Month-to-date summary page showing charges for several resources, with subtotal and total charges listed.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/billing/month-to-date-summary.4b8494f586d5521a13111c58dc1442651468c671874d83bb8f26f3f7991251e4.png)

In this section, you can:

- View the invoice in your browser, and expand details on the charges by resource type and individual resource
- Download a PDF of the invoice
- Download a CSV of the invoice with a more detailed breakdown of the charges, including which project each resource belongs to and their tags (comma-separated when a resource has more than one tag)

To download the PDF or CSV version of the invoice, click **Download**, then click **Download as PDF** or **Download as CSV**.

**Note**:

  Tag information in the CSV is included only for resource usage on or after 1 July 2026.

You can view past invoices in the **History** tab:

![Billing history table showing invoice dates, descriptions, and amounts for different months.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/billing/history.1f1357ec203436aec24934c8b28fa6790af80f92a8f946a67980957f1fcc18e4.png)

Like the month-to-date summary, you can similarly view historical invoices in your browser and download the PDF or CSV versions.

heading_path: Invoices > View and Download Invoices > Project Spend CSV File
title: Project Spend CSV File
content:
### Project Spend CSV File

**Note**:

  The project spend CSV file is currently in beta and is not yet available for all accounts.

The project spend CSV file contains estimates of your team spend by project.

This CSV file shows your current spend based on your actual usage, and doesn’t include any estimates of future usage for the current billing cycle. We calculate bandwidth by taking the total bandwidth charges for your team and dividing it each project’s usage.

heading_path: Invoices > Click here to expand an example of bandwidth charges in the project spend CSV file.
title: Click here to expand an example of bandwidth charges in the project spend CSV file.
content:
## Click here to expand an example of bandwidth charges in the project spend CSV file.

For example, say your team has currently accrued $100 of bandwidth overage charges across the following resources:

- 50% of the bandwidth usage is from a resource in Project A.
- 25% of the bandwidth usage is from another resource in Project A.
- 25% of the bandwidth usage is from a resource in Project B.

The project spend CSV file would summarize these charges in the following way:

```
Project,    Product,    Description,        USD
Project A,  Bandwidth,  Bandwidth Overage,  $75
Project B,  Bandwidth,  Bandwidth Overage,  $25
```

You can request a project spend CSV file from the Control Panel. On the [**Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing), in the **Month-to-date Summary** section, click **Request Project Spend CSV**. When you request a project spend CSV file, we send it to the email associated with your account.

title: View Credits
content:
## View Credits

When your team or organization has credits available, like credits from the [signup credit](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/signup-credit/index.html.md), the [**Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing) has a **Credits** section:

![Credits page showing available credits and a table listing an example credit with its expiration date, initial amount, and remaining balance.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/billing/credits.503d4649d759298120ae4f61e3f7546b562816b728135b46cbb68de5e2f13570.png)

This displays your team’s or organization’s available credits, their expiration, and their initial and remaining amounts.

Credit information is also displayed on invoices, including the month-to-date summary.

heading_path: Invoices > Create and View Purchase Orders
title: Create and View Purchase Orders
content:
## Create and View Purchase Orders

Purchase orders are a way to track your resource usage for your reference. When you add a purchase order to your team, that information appears on your invoices. You can also view the amounts invoiced to date and remaining against your purchase orders in the Control Panel.

**Note**:

  Purchase orders are for your reference, and do not function as usage or payment limits. If the full amount associated with a purchase order number is invoiced, or if the purchase order number otherwise expires or terminates, we take no action and continue to bill your primary payment method for your resource usage.

To add a purchase order to your team, on the **Billing** page, click the [**Settings** tab](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing/settings). In the **Purchase Orders** section, click **Create Purchase Order**.

In the window that opens, enter the purchase order number, amount, starting date, and optionally an ending date, then click **Save**. Your team’s active purchase orders are visible in an expandable table in this section:

![Purchase Orders page showing an active purchase order with its number, remaining amount, start and end dates, purchase order total, and invoiced-to-date amount.](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/billing/purchase-orders.4c127a46ea4f3a47fdbf5a816e6117bdcd6711c6674d273a402cc8c4fca48f18.png)

To cancel a purchase order, click the **…** menu next to the order you want to cancel, then click **Cancel Purchase Order**. In the window that opens, confirm the cancellation by entering the purchase order number and clicking **Cancel Purchase Order**. Your non-active purchase orders are also visible in the **Purchase Orders** section.

title: Invoice Limits
content:
## Invoice Limits

The following limits apply to invoices:

- We cannot change invoice and billing dates.
- Invoices do not reflect PayPal prepayments or credit/debit card payments. Invoices are not receipts for any such payments.
- We bill exclusively in USD and all invoices are in USD. We do not invoice in local currency.

In addition to monthly invoice emails, you can create [spend alerts](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/spend-alerts/index.html.md), which email you when your monthly spending crosses percentage thresholds of a budget you define.

title: Billing Spend by Date Range
content:
# Billing Spend by Date Range

The Spend by Date Range report provides a daily breakdown of your aggregated spend over a custom date range. You can view the report on the [**Insights** tab of the **Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing/insights).

The report groups spend by product (such as Droplets or Load Balancers) and lists your top individual resources. You can also retrieve raw daily spend data programmatically using the [Billing endpoints of the DigitalOcean API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/billing/index.html.md).

**Important**:

  The report and API provide spend data starting on 1 December 2025.

heading_path: Billing Spend by Date Range > View Spend by Date Range
title: View Spend by Date Range
content:
## View Spend by Date Range

On the **Billing** page, click the [**Insights** tab](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing/insights).

Select a month, a single day, or a custom date range to generate the report.

![The Billing Insights tab displaying the date range picker dropdown with a calendar view](https://docs.digitalocean.com/screenshots/billing/billing-insights-date-picker.4f26358873867d40486578307db77fdd044e507ecf105cdc9260068727951830.png)

The report aggregates spend using the following logic:

- **Product Grouping:** Spend is grouped by product type (for example, Droplets, Floating IPs, or Load Balancers).
- **Top Resources:** Within each product group, the report lists the top 100 resources by spend.
- **Rolled-up Resources:** Any remaining resources outside the top 100 are combined into a single line item (for example, “X unlisted resources”), which displays the total spend for those remaining items.

heading_path: Billing Spend by Date Range > Download a CSV Report
title: Download a CSV Report
content:
## Download a CSV Report

To download a CSV file containing the full list of resources for your selected date range, click **CSV** in the report. The CSV contains all resources, including those outside the top 100 shown in the control panel, along with the tags applied to each resource.

**Note**:

  Tag information in the CSV is included only for resource usage on or after 1 July 2026.

heading_path: Billing Spend by Date Range > Retrieve Spend Using the API
title: Retrieve Spend Using the API
content:
## Retrieve Spend Using the API

To retrieve raw daily spend data programmatically (JSON only), use the [`/v2/billing/{account_urn}/insights/{start_date}/{end_date}` endpoint](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/billing/index.html.md#billingInsights_list) of the DigitalOcean API.

heading_path: Billing Spend by Date Range > How to Retrieve Spend Data Using the DigitalOcean API
title: How to Retrieve Spend Data Using the DigitalOcean API
content:
## How to Retrieve Spend Data Using the DigitalOcean API

[Create a personal access token](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/create-personal-access-token/index.html.md) and save it for use with the API.

heading_path: Billing Spend by Date Range > How to Retrieve Spend Data Using the DigitalOcean API > cURL
title: cURL
content:
### cURL

Send a GET request to [`https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/billing/{account_urn}/insights/{start_date}/{end_date}`](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/billing/index.html.md#billingInsights_list).

Using cURL:

```shell
curl -X GET \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/billing/do:team:12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012/insights/2025-01-01/2025-01-31?per_page=20&page=1"
```

heading_path: Billing Spend by Date Range > How to Retrieve Spend Data Using the DigitalOcean API > Python
title: Python
content:
### Python

Using [PyDo](https://github.com/digitalocean/pydo), the official DigitalOcean API client for Python:

```python
import os
from pydo import Client

client = Client(token=os.environ.get("DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN"))

insights = client.billing.list_insights(
    account_urn="do:team:12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012",
    start_date="2025-01-01",
    end_date="2025-01-31",
    per_page=100,
    page=1
)
```

heading_path: Billing Spend by Date Range > Spend By Date Range Limits
title: Spend By Date Range Limits
content:
## Spend By Date Range Limits

The following limits apply to spend by date range reports:

- **Spend amounts are estimates.** The amounts shown in this report are estimates. Refer to your [monthly invoice](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/invoices/index.html.md) for final billing details.
- **Data is read-only.** The report and API provide read-only access to your billing data. You cannot modify billing information through this endpoint or through the **Insights** tab.

title: Signup Credit
content:
# Signup Credit

When you create your first team, DigitalOcean automatically applies a $5 signup credit. No promo code is required. The credit is visible in the Control Panel’s top navigation bar as a **Signup Credit** balance. The credit balance updates as you pay for resources.

The following conditions apply to the signup credit:

- Signup credits expire 90 days after signup.
- The credit applies to all products except SaaS Add-Ons.
- You must add a [valid payment method](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/manage-payment-methods/index.html.md) before you can create Droplets or other resources.
- You cannot transfer signup credits to other teams.
- Signup credits are subject to DigitalOcean’s [Promotional Credit & Discount Terms](https://www.digitalocean.com/legal/promotional-credit-discount-terms).

title: Bandwidth Billing
content:
# Bandwidth Billing

Details on bandwidth billing for DigitalOcean products are included on each product’s pricing page. The following sections summarize the same information for products that charge for bandwidth. There are no regional variations on bandwidth pricing.

Bandwidth billing is automated and you can view charges on [your invoice](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/invoices/index.html.md). Now in beta, you can additionally request a CSV file that has the details of your team’s bandwidth usage across Droplets, load balancers, and Kubernetes clusters. To request this file, on the **Billing** page, in the **Droplet Transfer (Bandwidth) Overview** section, click **Bandwidth Detail CSV (Beta)**.

title: Droplets
content:
## Droplets

Each Droplet plan includes an amount of free outbound data transfer. Additional outbound transfer is billed at $0.01 per GiB. Inbound transfer to Droplets is free.

Transfer allowance and usage is pooled cumulatively across all Droplets at the team level, not individually per Droplet. Accrued transfer does not roll over between months and cannot be transferred between teams.

Any data transfer sent by a Droplet using a public network interface counts against the transfer pool for that Droplet’s team. All IPv6 traffic uses the public interface. Data transfer between Droplets over the [VPC network](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/vpc/index.html.md) uses a private network interface. We do not bill for outbound data transfer that we determine is dropped by a DigitalOcean firewall rule.

In the **Droplet Transfer (Bandwidth) Overview** section of the [team billing page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing), you can view usage data and projections about your team’s transfer pool, updated daily. We base projections on the assumption that your team maintains the same daily averages for both quantity of active Droplets and bandwidth usage through the end of the billing cycle.

You can calculate bandwidth costs using our [Droplet bandwidth calculator](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tools/bandwidth).

heading_path: Bandwidth Billing > Droplets > Details and Examples
title: Details and Examples
content:
### Details and Examples

We bill Droplets for each second they exist, rounded to the nearest minute, up to a maximum of 2,419,200 seconds (28 days) per monthly billing cycle. For every second a Droplet exists, it accrues 1/2,419,200 of its total transfer allowance towards the team’s transfer pool, up to the maximum included with its plan.

For example, if a Droplet’s plan includes 1,000 GB of transfer allowance, the Droplet accrues 1,000 GB / 2,419,200 seconds, or about 0.0004 GB of transfer allowance per second towards the team’s transfer pool. If the team runs two such Droplets for an entire billing cycle, those Droplets accrue 2,000 GB of transfer allowance into the team’s transfer pool.

If the first Droplet uses 1,500 GB of outbound data transfer (which is more than it contributed to the pool) and the second Droplet uses 100 GB, they cumulatively used 1,600 GB of the team’s 2,000 GB transfer pool, so no overage fees apply.

title: App Platform
content:
## App Platform

Each App Platform plan includes an amount of [free outbound data transfer](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform/details/pricing/index.html.md#current-plans). Additional outbound transfer is billed at $0.02 per GiB. Inbound transfer to App Platform is free.

Transfer allowance and usage is pooled cumulatively across all apps at the team level, not individually per app or component. Accrued transfer does not roll over between months and cannot be transferred between teams.

You can [view ingress bandwidth](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform/how-to/view-insights/index.html.md) for individual apps, but you cannot currently view the accrued transfer allowance or cumulative usage for App Platform.

If the first app uses 800 GB of outbound data transfer (which is more than it contributed to the pool) and the second app uses 100 GB, they cumulatively used 900 GB of the team’s 1,000 GB transfer pool, so no overage fees apply.

title: Spaces
content:
## Spaces

Spaces subscriptions include 1,024 GiB of outbound data transfer (from Spaces buckets to the internet), which is shared between all buckets. Additional outbound transfer is $0.01 per GiB. Outbound data transfer is free in the following cases:

- From Spaces in NYC3 to Droplets in NYC1, NYC2, and NYC3
- From Spaces in SGP1 to Droplets in SGP1
- From Spaces in SFO2 to Droplets in SFO1, SFO2, and SFO3
- From Spaces in SFO3 to Droplets in SFO1, SFO2, and SFO3

- From Spaces in SYD1 to Droplets in SYD1
- From Spaces in BLR1 to Droplets in BLR1

heading_path: Bandwidth Billing > Spaces > Private Spaces Traffic
title: Private Spaces Traffic
content:
### Private Spaces Traffic

Droplets that use the [VPC-local DNS resolver](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/vpc/how-to/use-local-dns-resolver/index.html.md) can access Spaces buckets over DigitalOcean’s internal network instead of the public internet. When a Droplet resolves a Spaces URL through the VPC-local DNS resolver, the request is routed privately and does not count against your Spaces outbound transfer allowance.

Private Spaces traffic is available in all regions. In the following region groups, a Droplet can also access Spaces buckets in other datacenters within the same group over the internal network (for example, a Droplet in NYC1 accessing a bucket in NYC3):

- **AMS** (AMS2, AMS3)
- **NYC** (NYC1, NYC2, NYC3)
- **SFO** (SFO1, SFO2, SFO3)

Traffic between regions in different groups (for example, from a Droplet in NYC to a Spaces bucket in SFO) uses the public endpoint and is billed at the standard rate.

To use the private network route, your Droplet must be configured to use the [VPC-local DNS resolver](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/networking/vpc/how-to/use-local-dns-resolver/index.html.md). Droplets that use external DNS resolvers (such as Google or Cloudflare) resolve Spaces URLs to the public endpoint, and standard bandwidth billing applies.

Inbound bandwidth to Spaces never counts against your Spaces transfer allowance.

Droplets have their own transfer allowance, independent of Spaces. Traffic from Droplets to Spaces does not count against your Spaces transfer allowance (because inbound bandwidth to Spaces is free), but does currently count against your Droplets’ outbound transfer allowance.

Invoices include a breakdown of bandwidth usage and cost per Spaces bucket. If you have 100 or more Spaces buckets, you can only view this breakdown in the CSV version of the invoice. To view or download invoices, see our [Invoices billing page](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/invoices/index.html.md).

title: Kubernetes Worker Nodes
content:
## Kubernetes Worker Nodes

DOKS clusters accrue free bandwidth based on the worker pool’s largest sizes within 28 days of usage.

For example, if your worker pool has Droplets with a monthly bandwidth quota of 5 TB, then you accrue free bandwidth at the rate of `5 TiB/(24*28) * worker_pool_size = 7.44 GiB/hr * worker_pool_size`. For autoscaling clusters, the size of the worker pools vary.

title: Commitment Savings Plans
content:
# Commitment Savings Plans

Commitment savings plans are commitments to a consistent amount of usage with DigitalOcean over a period of time at a discounted rate. Refer to your contract for the full details of your commitment savings plan.

If your team has a commitment savings plan with DigitalOcean, it appears on your [invoice](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/invoices/index.html.md) as a discount along with any surcharge, if applicable.

You can also see your team’s commitment savings plans on [the **Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing), in the **Commitments Savings Plans** section. The table in this section lists your team’s active commitment savings plans. When you click the **+** to expand a commitment, it shows the following summary information:

- **Pre-Discount Amount**
- **Discount Percentage**
- **Post-Discount Amount**
- **Invoiced to Date**, which is your post-discount spend towards this commitment, excluding the current billing cycle’s usage to date
- **Commitment Details**

When a commitment expires, it no longer appears in the table.

title: Discounts
content:
# Discounts

Discounts reduce the price of a product or service. If you have a discount applied to your team, it appears on your [invoice](https://docs.digitalocean.com/platform/billing/invoices/index.html.md) as a line item with a description and the amount of the discount.

You can also see your team’s discounts on [the **Billing** page](https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/billing), in the **Discounts** section. The table in this section lists your team’s active discounts with the following information:

- **Discount**, which is the name of the discount
- **Start Month** and **End Month**
- **Discount Percentage**

When a discount expires, it no longer appears in the table.

Every Paperspace user has a Private Workspace with a unique namespace (your [username](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/accounts-and-teams/manage-accounts/index.html.md#username-namespace)). The Private Workspace is yours for your own Core and Gradient resources.

heading_path: Paperspace Accounts and Teams > Personal Accounts > Account Security
title: Account Security
content:
### Account Security

All aspects of the Paperspace platform are designed with security as the primary consideration, from the application layer all the way down to our data centers (for our hosted offerings).

- All Paperspace traffic is secured over a fully encrypted channel (SSL/TLS) independent of platform — web, desktop, or mobile.
- Traffic between our database, web servers, API, and internal networks is also encrypted (SSL/TLS)
- Our databases are secured with 256-bit AES or higher.
- We use 2,048 bit public keys in our certificates and support only high-strength symmetric ciphers.
- We monitor in real time for threats that could potentially impact our customer’s machine resources, and multiple password reset attempts locks your account.
- We employ a cloud operations team that monitors all aspects of security 24/7/365.

[How to Upload SSH Keys to Paperspace Personal Accounts](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/accounts-and-teams/add-ssh-keys/index.html.md): SSH keys provide a secure way to remotely access your Linux-based machines.

[How to Use and Manage Paperspace Secrets](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/accounts-and-teams/use-secrets/index.html.md): Use secrets to keep private keys secure while using Gradient.

content:
## Teams

Teams let you collaborate with people inside and outside of your organization. Teams are available at no cost and can be created and deactivated directly in the console. As a user, you can be a member of an unlimited number of teams.

heading_path: Paperspace Accounts and Teams > Teams > Team Roles
title: Team Roles
content:
### Team Roles

Team members can have one of two roles: admin or member. Roles determine a user’s level of access to a team’s shared resources, billing information, and settings.

| Role | Machines | Add-ons | Gradient Projects | Gradient Workloads | Billing Information | Team Settings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Admin** | Full access | Full access | Full access | Full access | Full access | Full access |
| **Member** | By assignment | No access | By assignment | Full access | No access | No access |

API keys are unique to the members who generated them. They can be generated by individual members, regardless of their role, but can be revoked by a team administrator.

heading_path: Paperspace Accounts and Teams > Teams > Team Emails
title: Team Emails
content:
### Team Emails

Emails that are sent exclusively to the team admins include:

- Operational alerts and maintenance notices
- Resource alerts, like billing alert policy notifications
- Emergency migration or reboot notices
- Receipts for upfront charges
- Invoices

Additionally, some team emails are sent only to specific members:

- Machine password emails are sent to the member that created the related machine.
- Support ticket emails are sent to members who participated in the support ticket.
- Quota increase approvals

heading_path: Paperspace Accounts and Teams > Teams > Team Quota (Service Limits)
title: Team Quota (Service Limits)
content:
### Team Quota (Service Limits)

Certain items within Paperspace are governed by *service limits*. These limits are visible on the **Billing** tab of the console.

If you need to increase a service limit, submit a [support ticket](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/machines/support/index.html.md), and then from the **Account Topic** dropdown menu, select **User Experience Increase**. From the **User Experience Issues** dropdown menu, select **Account Limits** option, and then fill out the rest of the ticket accordingly.

Tell us how you’re using Paperspace and how many machines you require so we can process your request effectively.

**Note**:

  When creating Core machines, you may be asked to **verify** your account which is distinct from Service Limits. Learn more about verification in the [Paperspace machines limits documentation](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/machines/details/limits/index.html.md).

title: Paperspace Pricing
content:
# Paperspace Pricing

All Paperspace resources are billed on a per-hour basis.

Non-GPU resources such as storage and public IP addresses have a maximum monthly charge. Once a non-GPU resource reaches its monthly maximum, it no longer incurs charges for the rest of the billing cycle.

Billing starts when you create a resource and ends when you destroy it.

heading_path: Paperspace Pricing > CPU and GPU Machines
title: CPU and GPU Machines
content:
## CPU and GPU Machines

Paperspace Machines are virtual machines for CPU and GPU workloads in the Paperspace console. Machines are billed hourly based on their hardware type and configuration. We do not charge for ingress or egress bandwidth for Paperspace Machines.

Machine compute charges apply only while a machine is powered on. When you shut down or power off a machine, compute billing stops for that machine. This differs from DigitalOcean Droplets, which are billed per second for as long as the Droplet exists. A powered-off Droplet continues to incur compute charges because its resources stay reserved until you destroy it. Paperspace Machines do not behave this way: shutting down a machine stops compute billing even though the machine still exists in your account.

When a Paperspace machine is powered off, attached storage, public IP addresses, and other add-ons continue to be billed on an hourly basis until you destroy those resources. To stop all charges for a machine and its add-ons, destroy the machine and any resources you no longer need.

You can view full technical specs for CPU, GPU, and multi-GPU machine types in the [Machine Type Reference](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/machines/details/machine-types/index.html.md).
